# 🐞 bug report

### Affected Package
Caused by [packages/compiler-cli/ngcc/src/packages/dependency_resolver.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/compiler-cli/ngcc/src/packages/dependency_resolver.ts)
### Description

At postinstall ngcc throw "imports|entry-points" errors on 3th party lib.
By example with angular-tree-component and ngx-virtual-scroller 3th party lib.

## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction
Simply run command: 
`ng new ap --minimal --defaults --skipInstall --enable-ivy && cd ap && npm i angular-tree-component && npm i ngx-virtual-scroller && npm install`

1. angular-tree-component : [Entry point 'angular-tree-component' contains deep imports into 'lodash/*...](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/packages/compiler-cli/ngcc/src/packages/dependency_resolver.ts#L138)

issue.body:
The support for decorators that were imported via a namespace,
e.g. `import * as core from `@angular/core` was implemented
piecemeal. This meant that it was easy to miss situations where
a decorator identifier needed to be handled as a namepsaced
import rather than a direct import.

One such issue was that UMD processing of decorators was not
correct: the namespace was being omitted from references to
decorators.

Now the types have been modified to make it clear that a
`Decorator.identifier` could hold a namespaced identifier,
and the corresponding code that uses these types has been
fixed.

Fixes #31394

body:
I think the difference is that one uses the static property style of decoration and the other uses the call helper style.

```js
    AriaDescriber.decorators = [
        { type: core.Injectable, args: [{ providedIn: 'root' },] },
    ];
```

vs

```js
        ActionsSubject = tslib_1.__decorate([
            core.Injectable(),
            tslib_1.__metadata("design:paramtypes", [])
        ], ActionsSubject);
```

I guess we only fixed it for the static property style.
